# ceryx_routes (Data Source)

Lists every route in Ceryx, including routes Terraform does not manage.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ceryx_routes" "all" {}

resource "ceryx_route" "app" {
  source = "app.example.com"
  target = "http://app:8000"
}

locals {
  managed   = toset([ceryx_route.app.source])
  unmanaged = setsubtract(data.ceryx_routes.all.sources, local.managed)
}

check "all_routes_managed" {
  assert {
    condition     = length(local.unmanaged) == 0
    error_message = "Routes not managed by Terraform: ${join(", ", local.unmanaged)}"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `routes` (Attributes List) Routes in the order Ceryx returns them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes))
- `sources` (Set of String) Source host names of all routes.

<a id="nestedatt--routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes`

Read-Only:

- `certificate_path` (String) TLS certificate path inside the Ceryx container, if set.
- `enforce_https` (Boolean) Whether plain HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS.
- `key_path` (String) TLS private key path inside the Ceryx container, if set.
- `mode` (String) `proxy` or `redirect`.
- `source` (String) Host name the route matches.
- `target` (String) Where requests go.
